name: pomp-against-pulse
style: English-spoken radio-play drama, voices talk rather than sing, gritty Yorkshire police-thriller score. Two clashing sound worlds. Inside the ambulance: thumping taiko pulse like a racing heart, a lone viola sawing raw, snarling dirty vintage synths, rain on metal, two-tone siren, rapid ECG bleeps; a breathless young Londoner woman in Multicultural London English and a worn-out gravel-voiced Sheffield bloke. Outside, the minister's limousine: the music sinks behind thick glass into a remote ceremonial parade, regal brass and cathedral organ, the only grandeur anywhere; one nasal, braying Etonian toff, petulant and spoilt. A long unbroken ECG whine closes it, followed by total quiet. Dry, close-miked, 14 seconds.
exclude: American accent, sung vocals, melody, chorus, rap, autotune, cheerful, comedic, upbeat pop, music after the flatline
lyrics:
[Intro: two-tone siren, taiko heartbeat, sawing viola, dirty synth]

[Shouted, young London woman, MLE]
Sixty over thirty! Fucking hurry up, we're gonna lose him!

[Shouted, weary Sheffield man]
Sats dropping, he's peri-arrest!

[Yelled, hoarse Northern driver]
Two minutes out! Get the fuck out of the way!

[Heartbeat drums halt, siren fades]

[Spoken, Sheffield man, bewildered]
Why have we stopped?!

[Distant regal brass and cathedral organ, heard through car glass]
[Spoken, braying Etonian toff, muffled]
I said raspberry-shaped hors d'oeuvres!

[Parade cuts dead, bleeps slow]
[Whispered, London woman]
Fifty over twen—

[Flatline]
[Silence]
[End]
